    68	\section{Key theorem forms}
    69	
    70	Throughout, $(q,m,d)$ is an admissible parameter tuple of the Pauli basis
    71	test, $\ket{\hat\psi}$ is the expanded state of the projective strategy
    72	under analysis, succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, and all
    73	approximations are with respect to $\ket{\hat\psi}$.  For lines
    74	$\ell_X, \ell_Z$ in $\F_q^m$, the POVM $\{T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\}$,
    75	with outcomes pairs of polynomials of degree at most $md$ on the two
    76	lines, is the two-basis combined line measurement, and
    77	$\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ is the combined point measurement; their
    78	consistency errors are $\delta_P = \poly(\eps, md/q)$ and
    79	$\delta_Q = \poly(\eps)$ respectively, and
    80	$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}} = \poly(\eps)$ is the line--point consistency
    81	error of the strategy.  The lemma under discussion asserts that a
    82	measurement $\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, built for each line $\ell$ in
    83	$\F_q^{2m+2}$, is $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$-consistent, on average over
    84	the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$, with the combined point
    85	measurement on the extended coordinates, together with the
    86	register-swapped counterpart.%
    87	\footnote{In the mirror of the source consulted here,
    88	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}: the
    89	lemma statement, with the error form $\poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$, is at
    90	lines~1020--1034 (label \path{lem:qld-4-13}); the central display with
    91	the first-route bound at lines~1134--1137
    92	(label \path{eq:qld-combined-lines-consistency}); the three claims at
    93	lines~1140--1239 (labels \path{claim:17-1}--\path{claim:17-3}); the
    94	second-route conclusion $O(m^2\delta_P)$ at lines~1241--1245, preceded by
    95	a duplicated sentence whose second copy carries a malformed reference;
    96	the product-distribution estimate invoked there at lines~1055--1061
    97	(label \path{eq:qld-xz-lines-restricted}); and the sub-line lemma at
    98	lines~1063--1116 (label \path{lem:qld-sublines}).}
    99	The comparison involves four forms of the error function
   100	$\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}(\eps,m,d,q)$.
   101	\begin{enumerate}
   102	  \item \textbf{Source form.}
   103	  $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}} = \poly(m^2\eps,\, md/q)$.  This is the form
   104	  printed in the statement.  Neither printed derivation supports it.
   105	  \item \textbf{Established form (first route).}
   106	  $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}
   107	  = O\big(m\,(\eps^{1/4} + \delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4}
   108	  + \delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2})\big)$, a function of the form
   109	  $m \cdot \poly(\eps,\, md/q)$.
   110	  \item \textbf{Second-route form (conditional).}
   111	  $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}} = O(m^2 \delta_P)
   112	  = m^2 \cdot \poly(\eps,\, md/q)$, conditional on a joint-law
   113	  decomposition that the sub-line lemma, as stated, does not provide.
   114	  \item \textbf{Consumer requirement.}  The unique consumer, the
   115	  polynomial-pair lemma, feeds $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$ into an error
   116	  of the form
   117	  $a(md)^a(\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ imported
   118	  from \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}; any bound
   119	  $m^{O(1)} \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$ is absorbed by enlarging $a$ and
   120	  shrinking $b$, so forms~2 and~3 both suffice downstream.
   121	\end{enumerate}

   123	\section{The domain of the conditional Lean helper}
   124	
   125	The source statement does not take an arbitrary joint point measurement as an
   126	input.  It uses the family $\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ constructed by the preceding
   127	point lemma, whose error has the form $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$.  Consequently,
   128	an internal theorem which accepts an already constructed point witness must retain
   129	the same quantitative dependency: it should first fix a function
   130	$\delta_Q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying the one-variable polynomial-error
   131	predicate, then choose $\delta_P$, and at strategy error $\eps$ accept only a
   132	point witness with bound $\delta_Q(\eps)$.
   133	
   134	Before the repair tracked by \ghissue{389}, the Lean helper
   135	\path{exists_combinedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness} instead had the quantifier
   136	order
   137	\[
   138	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   139	  \forall\eps\ \forall\delta_Q\ \forall Q,
   140	  \qquad Q\text{ has point error at most }\delta_Q
   141	  \Longrightarrow T\text{ has line error at most }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
   142	\]
   143	Thus the line-error function was chosen before an unrestricted scalar
   144	$\delta_Q$, and did not depend on it.  The fields of
   145	\path{CombinedPointsWitness} bound self-consistency and the two ordered-product
   146	comparisons by precisely this scalar; they impose no relation between an
   147	arbitrary $\delta_Q$ and $\eps$.  The conditioned-pasting estimate therefore
   148	cannot eliminate $\delta_Q$ from its conclusion.
   149	
   150	There is a concrete mathematical obstruction to the old domain.  Set
   151	$\eps=0$, take $m=1$ and fixed $d$, and let $q$ grow through admissible field
   152	sizes with $q>d+1$.  On any perfect strategy, define the supplied projective
   153	joint point measurement deterministically, with X answer $x^{d+1}$ and a fixed
   154	Z answer, identically on the two player sides.  Its self-consistency defect is
   155	zero, while the two ordered-product defects are finite and hence can be covered
   156	by a sufficiently large scalar $\delta_Q$, which the old helper quantified
   157	arbitrarily.  On an axis X line, however, every outcome allowed by
   158	\path{CombinedLinesWitness.axis_degree_X} evaluates as a polynomial of degree at
   159	most $d$.  Its difference from $x^{d+1}$ has at most $d+1$ roots, so even after
   160	mixing line outcomes the disagreement probability on that line is at least
   161	$1-(d+1)/q$.  Since axis lines have fixed positive weight in the line-point
   162	law, the resulting line consistency defect stays bounded away from zero as
   163	$q\to\infty$.  In contrast, the two-variable polynomial-error predicate forces
   164	$\delta_P(0,d/q)\to0$.  This argument diagnoses the theorem interface; no Lean
   165	counterexample theorem is asserted here.
   166	
   167	The repaired conditional helper has the form
   168	\[
   169	  \forall\delta_Q,\quad \delta_Q=\poly(\eps)\Longrightarrow
   170	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   171	  \forall\eps\ \forall Q\text{ with error }\delta_Q(\eps),\quad
   172	  \exists T\text{ with error }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
   173	\]
   174	This is not a new hypothesis on the paper theorem.  The source-facing Lean
   175	declaration \path{exists_combinedLinesWitness} preserves its original statement:
   176	it existentially obtains $\delta_Q$ and its point witnesses from the preceding
   177	point construction, then applies the conditional helper.
   178	
   179	The construction theorem is
   180	\path{combined_line_measurement_consistency}. For a joint point family
   181	with error $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$, it proves evaluated consistency
   182	of the explicit unconditioned measurement
   183	\[
   184	 T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
   185	 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
   186	\]
   187	under the original product of line-point distributions, with error
   188	$\delta_P(\eps,md/q)=\poly(\eps,md/q)$ and every directed opposite
   189	placement. The point-to-line comparisons at source lines 900--941 and the
   190	pasting argument at lines 942--961 supply the proof. The POVM,
   191	axis-degree properties, and X marginal of this same measurement are proved.
   192	
   193	The proof conditions the sampling law on the event that the X direction
   194	is nonzero, whose probability lies between $1/2$ and $1$. It leaves the
   195	measurement unchanged. On this event, the polynomial root bound gives the
   196	conditional collision estimate needed for pasting. Multiplication by the
   197	retained probability and addition of the discarded contribution, at most
   198	$1/(2q)$, restore the original product law. Thus the result concerns the
   199	unconditioned X-Z-X measurement, with no conditioning premise in its
   200	statement. The current heterogeneous pasting theorem requires only the two
   201	forward marginal comparisons, both supplied by the point-to-line estimates.
   202	
   203	The directly indexed auxiliary
   204	\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_established} then constructs the point
   205	witness internally, conditions the subline law on each extended line, and
   206	averages the polynomial combination of these actual paired-line effects.
   207	The real-part overlap estimates for both opposite placements give the
   208	corrected bound $C m\,\poly(\eps,md/q)$. This construction retains the
   209	completed answer alphabet and the directly indexed question law; it does not
   210	discharge their comparison with the printed source theorem.\footnote{The
   211	proof and its necessary dependencies were selectively recovered for
   212	\ghissue{512} from commit
   213	\path{6e8d67ef8ba22de69a0c166adcdf23ba6e7a33aa}, retained at
   214	\path{0f4ef05370350f4017439ebd839ef0561f13130f}. See
   215	\path{audits/2026-09-12_issue512-saved-proof-recovery.md} for the
   216	signature audit, axiom closure, and cumulative cost accounting.}

    35	/-- Completing the Pauli-answer measurement changes only outcome zero, where
    36	it adds the total effect of malformed answers. -/
    37	theorem completedPauliEffect_eq_raw_add_wrongForm {P : AdmissibleParams} {ι : Type*}
    38	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (M : Measurement (PauliAnswer P) ι)
    39	    (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P) :
    40	    (M.postprocess pauliAnswerOrZero).effect u =
    41	      M.effect (.pauliOutcome u) +
    42	        if u = 0 then ProjectiveSetting.wrongFormEffect (.pauli W) M else 0 := by
    43	  classical
    44	  rw [Measurement.postprocess_effect, ProjectiveSetting.wrongFormEffect,
    45	    Finset.sum_filter]
    46	  by_cases hu : u = 0
    47	  · subst u
    48	    simp only [ite_true]
    49	    calc
    50	      (∑ answer, if pauliAnswerOrZero answer = 0 then M.effect answer else 0) =
    51	          ∑ answer, ((if answer = .pauliOutcome 0 then M.effect answer else 0) +
    52	            (if validPauliAnswer (.pauli W) answer = false then M.effect answer else 0)) := by
    53	        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    54	        intro answer _
    55	        cases answer <;> simp [pauliAnswerOrZero, validPauliAnswer]
    56	      _ = _ := by
    57	        rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    58	        congr 1
    59	        · simp
    60	        · rw [← Finset.sum_filter]
    61	  · simp only [hu, ite_false, add_zero]
    62	    rw [Finset.sum_eq_single (.pauliOutcome u)]
    63	    · simp [pauliAnswerOrZero]
    64	    · intro answer _ hanswer
    65	      cases answer with
    66	      | value _ | alinePoly _ | dlinePoly _ | pairBits _ | bit _ | msTriple _ =>
    67	          simp only [pauliAnswerOrZero, ite_eq_right_iff]
    68	          intro hzero
    69	          exact (hu hzero.symm).elim
    70	      | pauliOutcome v =>
    71	          simp only [pauliAnswerOrZero, ite_eq_right_iff]
    72	          intro hv
    73	          exact (hanswer (by simp [hv])).elim
    74	    · simp

    81	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) :
    82	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (PauliEdge × PauliSpace P))
    83	        (fun ez => pauliRejectionAt S ez.1 ez.2) ≤ ε := by
    84	  have havg : avgOver (uniformDistribution (PauliEdge × PauliSpace P))
    85	      (fun ez => pauliRejectionAt S ez.1 ez.2) = 1 - S.value := by
    86	    rw [← rejectionEventAverage_eq_one_sub_value S]
    87	    unfold pauliBasisTest pauliQuestionDistribution
    88	    rw [Distribution.avgOver_map]
    89	    rfl
    90	  rw [havg]
    91	  linarith

    93	/-- Rejection on one fixed oriented edge is at most the number of edge types
    94	times the total rejection probability. -/
    95	theorem fixedEdgeRejection_le_error_of_win {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    96	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) (e : PauliEdge) :
    97	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (PauliSpace P)) (pauliRejectionAt S e) ≤
    98	      (Fintype.card PauliEdge : ℝ) * ε := by

   269	private theorem wrongFormEffect_ideal_norm_alice_le {P : AdmissibleParams}
   270	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S)
   271	    (W : PauliKind) (δ r : ℝ)
   272	    (hstate : ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealState P w.aux‖ ≤ δ)
   273	    (hmass : stateQForm S.ψ
   274	        (heteroKron
   275	          (ProjectiveSetting.wrongFormEffect (.pauli W) (S.A (pauliQuestion P W))) 1) ≤ r) :
   276	    ‖applyOperatorToState
   277	        (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   278	          (ProjectiveSetting.wrongFormEffect (.pauli W) (S.A (pauliQuestion P W))))
   279	        (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2 ≤ 2 * δ ^ 2 + 2 * r := by
   280	  let M : Measurement (PauliAnswer P) S.ιA := S.A (pauliQuestion P W)
   281	  let E := ProjectiveSetting.wrongFormEffect (.pauli W) M
   282	  let Q := liftedAEffect S (ιB' := w.ιB') w.φA E
   283	  let theta := isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ
   284	  let Delta := idealState P w.aux
   285	  let N := M.postprocess (validPauliAnswer (.pauli W))
   286	  have hE : E = N.effect false := by
   287	    exact wrongFormEffect_eq_validity_effect M W
   288	  have hEcontr : Eᴴ * E ≤ 1 := by
   289	    rw [hE]
   290	    exact MagicSquareRigidity.conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_effect N false
   291	  have hQcontr : Qᴴ * Q ≤ 1 := by
   292	    dsimp only [Q]
   293	    rw [raw_transfer_liftedAEffect_eq_tensor]
   294	    exact MagicSquareRigidity.conjTranspose_mul_le_one_leftTensor
   295	      (MagicSquareRigidity.conjTranspose_mul_le_one_conjIsometry w.φA hEcontr)
   296	  have htheta : ‖applyOperatorToState Q theta‖ ^ 2 ≤ r := by
   297	    dsimp only [Q, theta]
   298	    rw [raw_transfer_liftedAEffect_eq_tensor,
   299	      MagicSquareRigidity.applyOperatorToState_leftTensor_conjIsometry,
   300	      MagicSquareRigidity.norm_isometryTensor]
   301	    have hEpos : 0 ≤ E := by rw [hE]; exact N.pos false
   302	    have hEle : E ≤ 1 := by rw [hE]; exact measurement_effect_le_one N false
   303	    have hKpos : 0 ≤ heteroKron E (1 : Op S.ιB) :=
   304	      kronecker_nonneg hEpos (by simp)
   305	    have hKle : heteroKron E (1 : Op S.ιB) ≤ 1 := by
   306	      rw [← Matrix.one_kronecker_one]
   307	      exact kronecker_mono_left hEle (by simp)
   308	    rw [MagicSquareRigidity.norm_applyOperatorToState_sq]
   309	    have hKH : (heteroKron E (1 : Op S.ιB))ᴴ = heteroKron E 1 :=
   310	      (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp hKpos).isHermitian.eq
   311	    rw [hKH]
   312	    exact (quadratic_form_mono (MIPStarRE.Quantum.sq_le_self hKpos hKle) S.ψ).trans
   313	      hmass
   314	  have hdecomp : applyOperatorToState Q Delta =
   315	      applyOperatorToState Q (Delta - theta) + applyOperatorToState Q theta := by
   316	    simp [applyOperatorToState]
   317	  rw [hdecomp]
   318	  have hfirst : ‖applyOperatorToState Q (Delta - theta)‖ ≤ δ := by
   319	    exact (MagicSquareRigidity.norm_applyOperatorToState_le hQcontr _).trans (by
   320	      rw [norm_sub_rev]
   321	      exact hstate)
   322	  have htri := norm_add_le (applyOperatorToState Q (Delta - theta))
   323	    (applyOperatorToState Q theta)
   324	  have hsquare := pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _) htri 2
   325	  have hfirstsq := pow_le_pow_left₀
   326	    (norm_nonneg (applyOperatorToState Q (Delta - theta))) hfirst 2
   327	  nlinarith [sq_nonneg (‖applyOperatorToState Q (Delta - theta)‖ -
   328	    ‖applyOperatorToState Q theta‖)]

   391	/-- Alice's raw prescribed-answer distance is controlled by the completed
   392	distance, state error, and malformed-answer rejection mass. -/
   393	theorem raw_pauli_operator_distanceA_le_completed {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δ : ℝ}
   394	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value)
   395	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S)
   396	    (hstate : ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealState P w.aux‖ ≤ δ)
   397	    (W : PauliKind) :
   398	    rawPauliOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤
   399	      2 * pauliOperatorDistanceA P S w W + 4 * δ ^ 2 +
   400	        4 * (Fintype.card PauliEdge : ℝ) * ε := by
   401	  let M : Measurement (PauliAnswer P) S.ιA := S.A (pauliQuestion P W)
   402	  let E := ProjectiveSetting.wrongFormEffect (.pauli W) M
   403	  let bad := ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedAEffect S w.φA E)
   404	    (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   405	  have hmass := wrongFormPauliMass_alice_le_error S hwin W
   406	  have hbad : bad ≤ 2 * δ ^ 2 + 2 * (Fintype.card PauliEdge : ℝ) * ε := by
   407	    simpa only [bad, E, M, mul_assoc] using
   408	      wrongFormEffect_ideal_norm_alice_le S w W δ _ hstate hmass
   409	  have hpoint (u : PauliRegister P) :
   410	      ‖applyOperatorToState
   411	          (liftedAEffect S w.φA (M.effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   412	            pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2 ≤
   413	        2 * ‖applyOperatorToState
   414	          (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   415	              ((M.postprocess pauliAnswerOrZero).effect u) -
   416	            pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2 +
   417	          if u = 0 then 2 * bad else 0 := by
   418	    by_cases hu : u = 0
   419	    · subst u
   420	      rw [if_pos rfl, completedPauliEffect_eq_raw_add_wrongForm M W 0]
   421	      simp only [ite_true]
   422	      have hvec :
   423	          applyOperatorToState
   424	              (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   425	                  (M.effect (.pauliOutcome 0)) -
   426	                pauliProjOnA'' P W 0) (idealState P w.aux) =
   427	            applyOperatorToState
   428	                (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   429	                    (M.effect (.pauliOutcome 0) + E) -
   430	                  pauliProjOnA'' P W 0) (idealState P w.aux) -
   431	              applyOperatorToState (liftedAEffect S w.φA E)
   432	                (idealState P w.aux) := by
   433	        rw [raw_transfer_liftedAEffect_add]
   434	        simp only [applyOperatorToState, map_sub, LinearMap.sub_apply, map_add,
   435	          LinearMap.add_apply]
   436	        abel
   437	      rw [hvec]
   438	      have htri := norm_sub_le
   439	        (applyOperatorToState
   440	          (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   441	              (M.effect (.pauliOutcome 0) + E) -
   442	            pauliProjOnA'' P W 0) (idealState P w.aux))
   443	        (applyOperatorToState (liftedAEffect S w.φA E) (idealState P w.aux))
   444	      have hsquare := pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _) htri 2
   445	      dsimp only [bad]
   446	      nlinarith [sq_nonneg
   447	        (‖applyOperatorToState
   448	          (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   449	              (M.effect (.pauliOutcome 0) + E) -
   450	            pauliProjOnA'' P W 0) (idealState P w.aux)‖ -
   451	          ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedAEffect S w.φA E) (idealState P w.aux)‖)]
   452	    · rw [if_neg hu, completedPauliEffect_eq_raw_add_wrongForm M W u]
   453	      simp only [hu, ite_false, add_zero]
   454	      nlinarith [sq_nonneg
   455	        ‖applyOperatorToState
   456	          (liftedAEffect S w.φA (M.effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   457	            pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖]
   458	  unfold rawPauliOperatorDistanceA pauliOperatorDistanceA
   459	  change (∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   460	      ‖applyOperatorToState
   461	        (liftedAEffect S w.φA (M.effect (.pauliOutcome u)) - pauliProjOnA'' P W u)
   462	        (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2) ≤
   463	    2 * (∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   464	      ‖applyOperatorToState
   465	        (liftedAEffect S w.φA ((M.postprocess pauliAnswerOrZero).effect u) -
   466	          pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2) +
   467	      4 * δ ^ 2 + 4 * (Fintype.card PauliEdge : ℝ) * ε
   468	  calc
   469	    (∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   470	        ‖applyOperatorToState
   471	          (liftedAEffect S w.φA (M.effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   472	            pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2) ≤
   473	        ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   474	          (2 * ‖applyOperatorToState
   475	            (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   476	                ((M.postprocess pauliAnswerOrZero).effect u) -
   477	              pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2 +
   478	            if u = 0 then 2 * bad else 0) :=
   479	      Finset.sum_le_sum fun u _ => hpoint u
   480	    _ = 2 * (∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   481	          ‖applyOperatorToState
   482	            (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   483	                ((M.postprocess pauliAnswerOrZero).effect u) -
   484	              pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2) + 2 * bad := by
   485	      rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.mul_sum]
   486	      simp
   487	    _ ≤ 2 * (∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   488	          ‖applyOperatorToState
   489	            (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   490	                ((M.postprocess pauliAnswerOrZero).effect u) -
   491	              pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2) +
   492	          2 * (2 * δ ^ 2 + 2 * (Fintype.card PauliEdge : ℝ) * ε) := by
   493	      linarith
   494	    _ = _ := by

   342	## 7. The two printed claims recorded as non-asserted `Prop`s
   343	
   344	Two problematic source claims are retained as **`Prop`-valued definitions**.
   345	Declaring a proposition records its type; it does not assert or prove the
   346	proposition. Neither definition is consumed as a premise by `pauli_soundness`.
   347	They do not have identical status, however: the extended-lines definition
   348	preserves only the printed error expression on a corrected formal carrier,
   349	whereas the symmetric-attainment definition is intentionally referenced by a
   350	theorem refuting its universal form on the current Lean domain.

   194	\begin{proof}
   195	  \leanok
   196	  The strategy passes the diagonal lines test with probability $1-\gamma$.
   197	\end{proof}
   198	```

    24	## Pattern 1: Source-faithful statements and internal proof obligations
    25	
    26	### The rule
    27	
    28	A declaration presented as the formalization of a paper theorem, lemma,
    29	proposition, or corollary must state the paper result, up to faithful formal
    30	encoding of the mathematical domain.  Its public hypotheses and conclusion are
    31	both part of the statement.  Adding a load-bearing bridge, residual, repair,
    32	obligation-structure input, hypotheses bundle, or assumptions bundle not present
    33	in the cited statement changes the theorem into a conditional helper.
    34	
    35	The project therefore distinguishes three objects.
    36	
    37	| Object | Public statement | Blueprint status |
    38	|--------|------------------|------------------|
    39	| Paper theorem | Matches the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/` | May be linked by source-labelled `\lean{}`; statement-level `\leanok` only when the statement matches |
    40	| Internal proof obligation | Proves a missing intermediate mathematical input from paper hypotheses | May contain a tracked `sorry` while the proof is open |
    41	| Conditional helper | Quarantines an unproved intermediate obligation | Not a paper theorem; no source-labelled `\leanok` |
    42	
    43	It is never allowed to change the public statement of a declaration presented
    44	as the formalization of a source-labelled paper theorem.  At the final assembly
    45	point, the paper theorem must either discharge the extra hypotheses internally,
    46	or remain as the paper-aligned statement with an unfinished proof while the
    47	conditional helper is given a different name.
    48	
    49	The preferred way to expose unfinished work is a named internal theorem or
    50	definition with a precise paper-origin docstring and, if necessary, a tracked
    51	`sorry`.  This makes the proof frontier visible without weakening the statement
    52	of a source-labelled theorem.
    53	
    54	### Why legacy scaffolding may remain temporarily
    55	
    56	| Temporary reason | Explanation |
    57	|------------------|-------------|
    58	| **Localizing an obstruction** | A conditional helper can isolate the exact missing mathematical input while the obligation discharger is being proved. |
    59	| **Recovering useful proof content** | The proof body may contain genuine estimates or constructions that should be extracted into source-faithful lemmas. |
    60	| **Auditability** | An explicit temporary hypothesis is easier to find than an implicit assumption hidden in prose, provided it is named as proof debt. |
    61	
    62	These reasons do not justify strengthening a paper theorem.  They only explain
    63	why a short-lived helper declaration may exist while its remaining hypotheses
    64	are being actively removed.
    65	
    66	### How to proceed when a proof needs an extra input
    67	
    68	1. **Check the source statement.**  Read the corresponding TeX in
    69	   `references/ldt-paper/` before changing a theorem linked from the blueprint.
    70	2. **Keep the paper-facing declaration source-faithful.**  Boundary hypotheses
    71	   such as positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances, or
    72	   type-class assumptions may be faithful encodings when they are needed to
    73	   state the mathematics in Lean.  Proof data such as `BridgeInputs`,
    74	   `RepairInput`, `Residual`, `Package`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic
    75	   `Assumptions` is different: it is not a paper assumption unless the cited
    76	   statement says so.
    77	3. **Name the missing intermediate result.**  If the proof uses a mathematical
    78	   fact not yet formalized, state it as a separate proof obligation.  A
    79	   temporary `sorry` in this declaration is preferable to adding the obligation as
    80	   a hypothesis on the paper theorem.
    81	4. **Do not introduce conditional helpers by default.**  A helper whose name
    82	   ends in `_ofObligations` is a quarantine device, not a normal formalization
    83	   pattern.  It may remain temporarily only when it preserves substantial proof
    84	   content that cannot yet be connected to the paper hypotheses, has a tracked
    85	   discharge or deletion target, and has no source-labelled blueprint
    86	   `\leanok`.  If the helper would merely package missing work as an extra
    87	   hypothesis, restore the theorem with the paper statement and leave a tracked
    88	   `sorry` instead.
    89	5. **Audit the final statement.**  Every PR touching a source-labelled theorem
    90	   should compare paper assumptions and Lean assumptions, paper conclusion and
    91	   Lean conclusion, and report whether the Lean statement is exact, has only
    92	   faithful boundary hypotheses, or has extra assumptions.
    93	
    94	If a paper-facing declaration is temporarily proved by calling a conditional
    95	helper whose load-bearing input has not yet been produced from the paper
    96	hypotheses, the proof frontier must be marked explicitly.  The declaration
    97	should carry an `**Unfaithful:**` docstring section naming the non-paper
    98	dependency, citing the paper-gap note or tracking issue, and identifying the
    99	internal theorem that will remove the dependency.  A named proof obligation
   100	with a tracked `sorry` is preferred whenever possible, because it makes the
   101	missing mathematical assertion visible without adding it to the paper theorem
   102	statement.
   103	
   104	### Required metadata for new proof-obligation declarations
   105	
   106	A new declaration whose name contains a proof-debt token such as `Bridge`,
   107	`Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Producer`, `Input`, `Hypotheses`,
   108	`Assumptions`, `Obligation`, or `Witness` must explain its mathematical role in
   109	the def-site docstring.  A paper citation alone is not enough, because the
   110	reviewer must be able to tell whether the declaration is part of the paper
   111	statement or a Lean-only proof obligation.
   112	
   113	Use one of the following markers.
   114	
   115	| Marker | Use |
   116	|--------|-----|
   117	| `**Source:**`, `**Paper source:**`, or `**Source statement:**` | The declaration is a faithful formal encoding of a cited source statement or a field of that statement |
   118	| `**Faithful encoding:**` | The declaration records boundary data or domain data that the paper uses implicitly |
   119	| `**Proof obligation:**` or `**Internal proof obligation:**` | The declaration is a theorem or record that must be proved from the paper hypotheses before a source theorem is complete |
   120	| `**Conditional:**` | The declaration is a conditional helper; it must not be linked as the source theorem |
   121	| `**Unfaithful:**` | The declaration or proof currently depends on a load-bearing assumption not yet derived from the paper hypotheses |
   122	
   123	Proof-obligation, conditional, and unfaithful markers must cite a paper-gap note
   124	or tracking issue and must state the planned discharge or elimination theorem.
   125	If such a declaration would merely package missing work as an added hypothesis
   126	to a source theorem, do not introduce it; restore the source theorem statement
   127	and leave the missing proof as a tracked `sorry`.
   128	
   129	### Conditional helper boundary
   130	
   131	1. **Prefer a source theorem with a tracked `sorry`.**  If a proof requires a
   132	   construction that is not yet available from the paper hypotheses, the first
   133	   repair is to restore the source theorem statement and leave the missing proof
   134	   open.  Do not introduce a new `Input`, `Obligation`, `Residual`, `Repair`,
   135	   `Producer`, or `Package` merely to avoid that `sorry`.
   136	
   137	2. **Do not bundle several missing theorem-level steps into one hypothesis.**
   138	   The former Section 9 bundle `SelfImprovementObligations` and the helper
   139	   `selfImprovementFromObligations` were removed because they bundled
   140	   helper strong self-consistency, orthonormalization, and final-field transport
   141	   into a single route to the full self-improvement conclusion.  The correct
   142	   boundary is now the theorem `selfImprovement`, whose missing
   143	   proof is an explicit `sorry`.
   144	
   145	   The former induction-section helper
   146	   `selfImprovementInInductionSection_ofObligations` was removed because it
   147	   encouraged propagation of the Section 9 bundle into the Section 6 successor
   148	   constructors.  Those constructors now call the theorem
   149	   `selfImprovementInInductionSection` directly; its current proof gap is the
   150	   correct place for the missing work.
   151	
   152	3. **Propagation is a warning sign.**  The consumer of
   153	   `selfImprovementInInductionSection` — typically a
   154	   `MainInductionStep` theorem — should close the hypothesis with an internal
   155	   theorem as soon as possible.  If the hypothesis propagates upward toward a
   156	   paper-labelled theorem, the PR should stop and either prove the obligation or
   157	   restore the paper theorem with an explicit unfinished proof.
   158	
   159	4. **Final closure at the paper theorem.**  The theorem `mainFormal` in
   160	   `MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/MainTheorem/MainFormal.lean` is reserved for the
   161	   paper-shaped statement.  If the witness needed by the final transport has
   162	   not yet been constructed from the paper hypotheses, the theorem should remain
   163	   an explicit unfinished proof.  Do not replace the missing construction by
   164	   extra bridge, residual, repair, package, or obligation hypotheses, and do not
   165	   proliferate named obligation declarations merely to avoid a direct `sorry`.
   166	
   167	   The paper-labelled `mainFormal` should have the hypotheses of the paper
   168	   theorem: a projective strategy passing the low individual degree test, the
   169	   stated parameter bounds, and the faithful formalization of the ambient
   170	   domains.  Bridge, residual, repair, and proof-obligation inputs must be
   171	   produced inside its proof rather than added to its statement.
   172	
   173	### Existing bridge-like declarations
   174	
   175	Several older declarations still name proof obligations explicitly.  They are
   176	transitional proof debt, not a pattern to extend to paper theorem statements.
   177	When such a declaration remains useful, its role should be made explicit and
   178	kept away from source-labelled blueprint entries.
   179	
   180	| Declaration | Status to maintain |
   181	|-------------|--------------------|
   182	| `LdPastingNontrivialContext` | Nontrivial-regime context for `ldPastingNontrivial`; do not present it as the unrestricted `thm:ld-pasting` context |
   183	| `Pasting.ldPastingNontrivial` | Restricted nontrivial-regime form of `thm:ld-pasting`; link from a Lean-only remark, while `Pasting.ldPasting` remains the unrestricted source-facing theorem |
   184	
   185	The former same-carrier `mainFormal` transport-witness route has been retired.
   186	The former `SelfImprovement.HelperStrongSelfConsistencyInput`,
   187	`SelfImprovement.OrthonormalizationInput`, `SelfImprovement.FinalFieldsInput`, and
   188	`MakingMeasurementsProjective.OrthonormalizationInput` bundles have been removed.
   189	Useful proof content should be kept as named construction lemmas, while missing
   190	orthonormalization or final-field arguments remain direct proof gaps on the
   191	source-facing theorem until proved from the paper hypotheses.
   192	
   193	The former `MakingMeasurementsProjective.SpectralTruncationInput` abbreviation
   194	has likewise been retired.  The spectral-truncation step is represented by the
   195	source-shaped statement `SpectralTruncationStatement` and by direct construction
   196	theorems such as `spectralTruncationStatement_of_sourceAlmostProjective`,
   197	rather than by an `Input` wrapper passed through later theorems.
   198	
   199	### Retiring auxiliary declarations
   200	
   201	An auxiliary declaration should be removed from the main blueprint route, or
   202	renamed and documented as a purely internal lemma, when all of the following
   203	conditions hold.
   204	
   205	1. It is not a statement in the cited paper and is not an explicitly cited
   206	   outside result.
   207	2. No current proof of a paper-level target needs it as stated.
   208	3. It assumes stronger proof data, finite-length data, completion data, repair
   209	   data, synchronization data, or package fields than the paper proof requires.
   210	
   211	If such a declaration is still useful as a formal intermediate result, keep it
   212	as a lemma or a visibly conditional helper with a planned discharge.  It should
   213	not remain a headline replacement for the paper theorem, and it should not be
   214	the target of a source-labelled blueprint `\leanok`.
   215	
   216	### Former proof obligations in `MainFormal.lean`
   217	
   218	The former direct tracked proof obligations in `MainFormal.lean` and the
   219	Section 6 successor route have been discharged under the corrected source
   220	statements.  The theorem `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` is the corrected
   221	two-space source theorem.  The earlier same-carrier auxiliary interface has
   222	been retired; the headline theorem carries no bridge, residual, repair,
   223	package, producer, generic hypothesis, or proof-obligation input in its public
   224	statement.
   225	
   226	### Distinction from anti-patterns
   227	
   228	This rule addresses the same risk as conclusion-shaped-hypothesis smuggling
   229	(anti-pattern A1 in `docs/anti_patterns.md`), but it is stricter for
   230	paper-labelled declarations:
   231	
   232	- A conclusion-shaped hypothesis is always unacceptable.
   233	- A genuine intermediate fact may appear only in a separately named conditional
   234	  helper while its obligation discharger is being proved.
   235	- That same intermediate fact is still unacceptable as an added hypothesis on
   236	  the public statement of the paper theorem, unless it is a faithful encoding
   237	  of a hypothesis present in the cited source.
   238	
   239	Obligation structures that bundle still-unproved theorem-level steps are proof
   240	debt under this pattern.  They should not be introduced merely because a proof
   241	is blocked.  The preferred repair is to keep the paper-labelled statement
   242	source-faithful and make the exact missing mathematical step visible as a named
   243	lemma or as a `sorry` in the theorem with the paper statement.

   247	## Pattern 2: Blueprint–Lean synchronization
   248	
   249	### The three tags
   250	
   251	The blueprint (under `blueprint/src/chapter/`) uses three LaTeX commands
   252	to link to Lean:
   253	
   254	| Tag | Meaning | Example |
   255	|-----|---------|---------|
   256	| `\lean{Name}` | The corresponding Lean declaration exists | `\lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal}` |
   257	| `\leanok` (statement-level) | The Lean declaration compiles and its statement matches the source or blueprint statement; it does not certify proof closure | `\leanok` |
   258	| `\leanok` (proof-level) | The proof block is fully formalized — the theorem or lemma has a complete sorry-free proof | `\lean{...}` plus `\leanok` inside `\begin{proof}` |
   259	| `\uses{label}` | The statement or proof block depends on the cited result | `\uses{thm:orthonormalization, prop:completing-to-measurement}` |
   260	
   261	Do not use statement-level `\leanok` for a source-labelled theorem whose Lean
   262	declaration is conditional on bridge, residual, repair, proof-obligation input,
   263	generic hypotheses bundle, or generic assumptions bundle
   264	data not present in the source.
   265	
   266	### Why some nodes show white in the dep graph
   267	
   268	The dependency graph at
   269	`https://LionSR.github.io/MIPStarRE/blueprint/dep_graph_document.html`

   272	- **Green**: proof-level `\leanok` is present (the proof block is fully formalized)
   273	- **White** (or white-border): `\lean{}` exists but proof-level `\leanok` is absent; may carry a statement-level `\leanok` during staged development
   274	- **Gray**: No `\lean{}` tag

   303	### The `\uses{}` convention
   304	
   305	`\uses{}` should appear:
   306	
   307	- On **statement blocks** (theorem/lemma/definition environments): only
   308	  to record *mathematical* dependencies — other definitions or theorems
   309	  whose statements are used in *stating* the current result (not in
   310	  proving it).
   311	- On **proof blocks** (`\begin{proof}`): to record which lemmas are
   312	  invoked in the proof.  This is the natural home for lemma-citation
   313	  chains.
   314	
   315	A common mistake is placing proof-only `\uses{}` on statement blocks.
   316	For the checklist item in the review:
   317	`docs/blueprint_style_guide.md` covers this in the section on
   318	`\uses{}` placement.

   325	```
   326	
   327	The CI linting step effectively runs `leanblueprint web` from the
   328	`blueprint/` directory.  After adding or removing `\leanok` tags,
   329	always run this locally to verify the graph updates.

1	# Mathematical Language Guidelines
     2	
     3	MIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing
     4	the formalization with the paper and blueprint.
     5	
     6	This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
     7	naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
     8	`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.
     9	
    10	## Scope
    11	
    12	These guidelines apply to:
    13	
    14	- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
    15	- module docstrings;
    16	- declaration docstrings;
    17	- documentation-visible section comments;
    18	- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
    19	- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
    20	- issue titles and issue bodies;
    21	- PR titles and PR descriptions.
    22	
    23	## Source of Truth
    24	
    25	Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:
    26	
    27	1. `references/ldt-paper/`
    28	2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
    29	3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files
    30	
    31	When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
    32	example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
    33	projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.
    34	
    35	## Reference Notation And Terminology
    36	
    37	The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
    38	reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
    39	docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
    40	without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.
    41	
    42	When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
    43	location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
    44	first applicable location in the following order:
    45	
    46	1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
    47	   differs from the paper;
    48	2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
    49	   family of declarations in that file;
    50	3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
    51	   blueprint;
    52	4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
    53	   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.
    54	
    55	The explanation should say:
    56	
    57	- the notation or term used in the paper;
    58	- the Lean object or name which represents it;
    59	- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
    60	- the scope in which the replacement should be used.
    61	
    62	A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
    63	where future readers can learn it.
    64	
    65	Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
    66	should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
    67	rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.
    68	
    69	## Naming Norm
    70	
    71	Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
    72	conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
    73	assembled.
    74	
    75	Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
    76	`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
    77	uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
    78	such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
    79	clearer phrase.
    80	
    81	This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
    82	Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
    83	blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
    84	mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
    85	number, or implementation history.
    86	
    87	### Concrete examples
    88	
    89	The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
    90	codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
    91	others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
    92	process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
    93	assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
    94	paper or blueprint would recognize.
    95	
    96	| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
    97	|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
    98	| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
    99	| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
   100	| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
   101	| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
   102	| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
   103	| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
   104	| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
   105	| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
   106	| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
   107	| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |
   108	
   109	An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
   110	phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
   111	In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.
   112	
   113	File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
   114	named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
   115	exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.
   116	
   117	### Shared helpers
   118	
   119	When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
   120	more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
   121	shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
   122	ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
   123	call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.
   124	
   125	Procedure:
   126	
   127	1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   128	   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   129	   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   130	   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   131	   explicit argument.
   132	2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   133	   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   134	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   135	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   136	   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
   137	3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   138	   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
   139	4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   140	   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   141	   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   142	   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   143	   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   144	   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
   145	5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   146	   blueprint location it supports.
   147	
   148	### Legacy identifier treatment
   149	
   150	If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
   151	describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
   152	identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
   153	in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.
   154	
   155	Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   156	public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
   157	shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
   158	blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.
   159	
   160	## Review Checklist
   161	
   162	Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
   163	documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.
   164	
   165	- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
   166	      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
   167	      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
   168	      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
   169	      implementation-phase labels)?
   170	- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
   171	      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
   172	      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
   173	      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
   174	      source does not use them that way?
   175	- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
   176	      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
   177	      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
   178	      that order of preference?
   179	- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
   180	      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
   181	      construction they support?
   182	- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
   183	      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
   184	      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
   185	- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
   186	      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
   187	      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
   188	      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
   189	- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
   190	      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
   191	      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
   192	      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.
   193	
   194	Review-fix PRs touching a surface covered by an active audit should read the
   195	relevant audit before changing names or prose.

     1	# Lean Proof-Evasion Anti-Patterns
     2	
     3	Catalog of subtle proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks
     4	(`sorry`-free, no forbidden tactics, all axioms standard) yet still fail to
     5	prove the claimed mathematics. Complements
     6	the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference, which covers the kernel-level
     7	blockers; this file covers patterns where the Lean code *compiles and the
     8	trick is at the level of what the statement says or what the definitions
     9	bake in*.
    10	
    11	Every pattern here is **castle-in-the-air in spirit**: a theorem named after a
    12	paper result that doesn't actually prove it. The named offenders below all
    13	cross-reference a concrete issue or PR so reviewers can see a real example.
    14	
    15	## Why this matters
    16	
    17	Kernel checks are necessary but not sufficient. A theorem can:
    18	
    19	- Be marked `\leanok` in the blueprint,
    20	- Have a sorry-free proof body,
    21	- Have a clean axiom closure (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only),
    22	
    23	and still prove **nothing that the paper actually claims**, if the proof
    24	obligation has been displaced into a hypothesis, a definition, or a sentinel
    25	branch. The patterns below are the displacement mechanisms we've seen in this
    26	codebase.
    27	
    28	## Catalogue
    29	
    30	- [A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis](#a1--conclusion-shaped-hypothesis)
    31	- [A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand](#a2--definitional-sleight-of-hand)
    32	- [A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions](#a3--zero-fallback-branches-hiding-preconditions)
    33	- [A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials](#a4--trivial-default-witnesses-for-existentials)
    34	- [A5 — Castle-in-the-air / bypassing Mathlib](#a5--castle-in-the-air--bypassing-mathlib)
    35	- [A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles](#a6--external-statement-smuggles)
    36	
    37	---
    38	
    39	## A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis
    40	
    41	**Smell.** The theorem takes a hypothesis whose type is the theorem's own
    42	conclusion (or an `∃`/function that produces the conclusion). The proof body
    43	is a trivial `rcases`/`exact`/`.trans`/`simpa using h` and does no
    44	mathematical work. A variant wraps the hypothesis in a named bundle
    45	(`*BridgePackage`, `*Statement`); see issues [#449], [#451], [#477] for the
    46	catalogue, and [#493] for the inline-existential mutation triggered by
    47	PR [#491].
    48	
    49	### Why it's bad
    50	
    51	The theorem's named mathematical content is never derived from prior lemmas;
    52	the caller (who supplies the hypothesis) has to discharge it. In practice the
    53	caller then has the same problem, pushing the obligation further up the
    54	stack. The theorem is true under a vacuous hypothesis and the `\leanok` tag
    55	misrepresents the actual state of the proof.
    56	
    57	### How to spot it
    58	
    59	- The hypothesis type contains, up to `∃` / `∧` / a coercion, the theorem's
    60	  conclusion.
    61	- The proof body is one of:
    62	  - `rcases h with ⟨...⟩; exact ⟨...⟩`
    63	  - `exact h.fieldName` / `exact h.a.trans h.b`
    64	  - `by simpa using h.fieldName`
    65	- The hypothesis is a bundle named `*BridgePackage`, `*Witness`, `*Package`,
    66	  `*Output`, with a field whose type matches the conclusion structure.
    67	- Consumers of the bundle are trivial (field projection + return).
    68	
    69	### Concrete example
    70	
    71	Historical example (before the MainInductionStep cleanup):
    72	
    73	```lean
    74	theorem mainInduction
    75	    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    76	    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)
    77	    (eps delta gamma : Error) (k : ℕ)
    78	    (hbridge : MainInductionBridgePackage params strategy eps delta gamma k) :
    79	    ∃ G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι,
    80	      ConsRel strategy.state ...
    81	        (mainInductionError params k eps delta gamma) := by
    82	  rcases hbridge.witness with ⟨error, G, hG, herror⟩
    83	  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩
    84	  exact ⟨le_trans hG.offDiagonalBound herror⟩
    85	```
    86	
    87	Here `MainInductionBridgePackage.witness` has type
    88	`∃ error, ∃ G, ConsRel ... error ∧ error ≤ mainInductionError ...` — literally
    89	the conclusion. The code has since been refactored to remove both this
    90	specific MainInductionStep bridge and the interim theorem alias that exposed
    91	the same witness shape under the paper theorem's name, but the snippet remains
    92	the archetypal example of the anti-pattern.
    93	
    94	PR [#491] proposed to delete the `*BridgePackage` by **inlining** the bundle's
    95	fields as explicit hypotheses. That only scatters the same pattern across
    96	individual signatures without producing any proof — it's strictly worse
    97	because the named bundle at least shows up in one tracker. Do not accept PRs
    98	that discharge an ungrounded bridge by flattening it into conclusion-shaped
    99	existential hypotheses, or by reintroducing the same shape under a theorem name
   100	that suggests the paper result has been proved.
   101	
   102	### How to fix it
   103	
   104	Prefer **proving a real intermediate lemma** — one that the paper also uses
   105	— and stating its signature with the paper's hypotheses (not the theorem's
   106	conclusion). Then use it inside the larger theorem. If the missing content
   107	cannot be formalized yet, state the missing assertion as a named obligation
   108	to be proved from the paper hypotheses, and leave the corresponding proof open
   109	under a tracker. Do not put that obligation on the source-labelled theorem as
   110	an extra hypothesis. Existing `BridgePackage`-style declarations are proof
   111	debt to be removed or converted into source-faithful obligations; they are not
   112	the preferred shape for new work.
   113	
   114	A signature passes the smell test if:
   115	
   116	- Every hypothesis is a **named intermediate fact** that also appears in the
   117	  paper or blueprint proof, not the theorem's output packaged up, and
   118	- Replacing a hypothesis with its negation would produce a *different*
   119	  theorem, not a trivially-false one.

   132	
   133	## A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand
   134	
   135	**Smell.** A `def`/`abbrev` is written so its body is the paper's claim, and
   136	a nearby `theorem` restates that claim and proves it by `rfl` (or a one-line
   137	`simp [foo]` where `foo` is the defining equation). The "mathematical
   138	content" has been baked into the definition; the theorem is a tautology. See
   139	issues [#477], [#494].
   140	
   141	### Why it's bad
   142	
   143	`rfl` proves that a definition equals itself. If the definition is chosen
   144	*so that* it equals the conclusion, the `rfl` "proof" transports none of the
   145	paper's reasoning — it is literally the reflexivity of a shape we invented to
   146	match the conclusion. The real identity the paper proves (e.g.,
   147	`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ` over an actual inner product) is still not stated
   148	anywhere in Lean.
   149	
   150	### How to spot it
   151	
   152	- A `theorem` whose body is `rfl` / `by rfl` / `by simp [defName]` where
   153	  `defName` is the def that unfolds to the conclusion.
   154	- A `structure` with a `Prop`-typed field whose *role* in the paper is a
   155	  nontrivial identity (SVD, orthonormality, Cauchy–Schwarz), accompanied by a
   156	  constructor that discharges that field with `rfl`.
   157	- A `def foo := if α = β then 1 else 0` followed by a theorem asserting
   158	  `foo α β = if α = β then 1 else 0`.
   159	- Bridge-like structures where every field is itself a function
   160	  `(precondition) → (conclusion-step)` and the consumer applies the field
   161	  directly.
   162	
   163	### Concrete example
   164	
   165	From `MIPStarRE/LDT/ExpansionHypercubeGraph/Defs/Fourier.lean`:
   166	
   167	```lean
   168	/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/
   169	def fourierBasisInnerProduct (params : Parameters)
   170	    (α β : Point params) : Error :=
   171	  if α = β then 1 else 0
   172	
   173	/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/
   174	lemma fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq (params : Parameters)
   175	    (α β : Point params) :
   176	    fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0 := rfl
   177	
   178	/-- `prop:eigenvectors`. -/
   179	theorem eigenvectors (params : Parameters) :
   180	    (∀ α β : Point params,
   181	      fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0) ∧ ... := by
   182	  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
   183	  · intro α β
   184	    exact fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq params α β    -- castle: def IS Kronecker delta
   185	  ...
   186	```
   187	
   188	The paper's orthonormality claim — that the additive characters `φ_α` form an
   189	orthonormal basis under the actual inner product
   190	`⟨f, g⟩ := (1/|V|) · ∑_u f(u)^* · g(u)` — requires a genuine character-sum
   191	identity. The Lean theorem states and proves only the trivial fact that the
   192	definition equals itself.
   193	
   194	### Not every `rfl` is a castle
   195	
   196	Distinguish from legitimate bookkeeping where a named equation is literally
   197	how something was defined. Example: `mainFormalError_eq_envelope` in
   198	`Test/ErrorCascade/Definitions.lean` unfolds the definition of
   199	`mainFormalError` to its envelope factorization. The mathematical content is
   200	elsewhere (the envelope is derived from per-step bounds); the `rfl` theorem is
   201	a naming convenience only. The test is: **does the `def` body encode a paper
   202	identity, or does it just name a compound expression?**
   203	
   204	### How to fix it
   205	
   206	1. Move the paper's real definition to the concrete one: for Fourier, define
   207	   the inner product as the actual sum over vertices, and the characters
   208	   `φ_α` as functions from `Point params` to `ℂ`.
   209	2. State the paper's identity (`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ`) as a theorem over those
   210	   concrete objects.
   211	3. Prove it via the standard character-sum derivation (or cite the Mathlib
   212	   counterpart if one exists — `Matrix.dotProduct` / `Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff`
   213	   combined with `ZMod.sum_pow_units` style lemmas).
   214	4. If you want to keep the Kronecker shorthand, define it *afterward* as a
   215	   consequence, not as the primitive.

   224	## A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions
   225	
   226	**Smell.** A total function is defined by `if eligible then real_value else
   227	default`, where the `default` (usually `0`, `default`, `⊥`, or
   228	`Classical.arbitrary`) is a sentinel for "precondition not met." Downstream
   229	theorems state properties that are only true on the eligible branch, but the
   230	theorem's type signature does not carry the eligibility proof, so the
   231	obligation moves silently from the prover to whoever happens to call the
   232	function. See issue [#495], related to [#307].
   233	
   234	### Why it's bad
   235	
   236	The signature lies about the domain of validity. A caller passing a
   237	non-eligible input gets `0` back; any theorem proved about "the output" is
   238	proved for `0`, which is trivially true and carries no information. When a
   239	later theorem composes the output with another lemma, the composition
   240	type-checks but the conclusion is vacuous on inputs where the original
   241	precondition failed.
   242	
   243	The paper, by contrast, restricts the quantifier in the first place:
   244	"Fix a tuple `(x₁, ..., x_k)` with Hamming weight `≥ d+1`." The Lean should
   245	match.
   246	
   247	### How to spot it
   248	
   249	- `match ... with | some _ => real | none => 0` or `| _ => 0`.
   250	- `if hEligible : P then ... else default`.
   251	- Identifier names containing `fallback`, `placeholder`, `sentinel`,
   252	  `dummy`, `or0`, `orDefault`.
   253	- Recursive definitions whose base case unconditionally returns a sentinel.
   254	- Functions that return `Polynomial params` but can return the zero polynomial
   255	  on inputs that shouldn't be in the domain.
   256	
   257	### Concrete example (historical; resolved by PR #561)
   258	
   259	Until PR #561, `MIPStarRE/LDT/Pasting/Defs/Interpolation.lean` contained:
   260	
   261	```lean
   262	/-- Extract the polynomial from a completed slice outcome; returns 0 on ⊥. -/
   263	noncomputable def extractSliceOr0 {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   264	    (g : GHatOutcome params) : PolynomialModel params :=
   265	  match g with
   266	  | some p => p.poly
   267	  | none   => 0
   268	```
   269	
   270	The consumer `interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport` ran Lagrange
   271	interpolation on `extractSliceOr0`-extracted values. If the support contained
   272	a `none`, the interpolant silently pretended that slice evaluated to zero.
   273	The paper's Lagrange step is quantified over *eligible* slices only, so the
   274	Lean API should carry `∀ i ∈ support, (g i).isSome` as a hypothesis; instead
   275	it carried nothing, and the theorem technically type-checked on inputs for
   276	which its conclusion was meaningless.
   277	
   278	**Current status:** resolved. The live API now removes `extractSliceOr0`,
   279	threads the explicit hypothesis `hσsupport : σ ⊆ gHatTupleSupport gs` into
   280	`interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport`, and packages the chosen support subset
   281	as `InterpolationSupportWitness` so the arbitrary choice and its proof fields
   282	are visible at call sites.
   283	
   284	### Acceptable uses of this pattern
   285	
   286	Not every default branch is a castle. `Inhabited` / `Nonempty` instances
   287	that provide a canonical inhabitant (e.g., the zero polynomial for
   288	`Nonempty (Polynomial params)`) are plumbing, not proof. The test is: **does
   289	any theorem mention the output?** If a theorem says "the output satisfies
   290	P", and P is not trivially satisfied by the sentinel, the fallback is
   291	smuggling a precondition.
   292	
   293	### How to fix it
   294	
   295	Pick one of:
   296	
   297	1. **Make the precondition explicit.** Add `(h : eligible input) :` to the
   298	   signature. Let Lean's type system enforce that non-eligible inputs cannot
   299	   be passed.
   300	2. **Return an `Option`.** The `none` result forces every caller to handle
   301	   the case, so theorems about "the output" now quantify only over the
   302	   `some` branch.
   303	3. **Restrict the domain.** Instead of `(x : X) → Y`, take `(x : {x : X //
   304	   P x}) → Y`. Common for finite-support Lagrange-style constructions where
   305	   the subtype is computable via `Finset.filter`.
   306	
   307	### Classical-logic dependencies
   308	
   309	A sibling smell in this pattern: `DecidablePred` / `DecidableEq` instances
   310	that silently use `Classical.dec` to fill in decidability that should be
   311	constructive. The historical `interpolationEligibleSandwichFamily`
   312	implementation was exactly such a case: it used `open Classical in ...` to
   313	gate a predicate that is actually decidable by a finite-support check. PR
   314	#561 fixed that example by adding `interpolationEligible_decidablePred`.
   315	Those classical instances are acceptable only when the predicate is genuinely
   316	non-constructive; if a constructive instance is plausible, write it, don't
   317	bottom out in `Classical.dec`. See [#495] for the full catalogue of
   318	classical-logic uses in `LDT/Pasting/`.

1	# The ITP artifact
     2	
     3	This page is for two audiences: a **reviewer** who received the artifact
     4	tarball and wants to check that the claimed theorems really are proved, and a
     5	**maintainer** who has to cut the next snapshot.
     6	
     7	The artifact is a **release snapshot of the mathematical development**, not the
     8	working repository. It is produced by `scripts/make_artifact.sh` from a tagged
     9	commit, and every copy carries a `MANIFEST.txt` naming the commit it came from.
    10	
    11	## What is in it
    12	
    13	| path | what it is |
    14	|---|---|
    15	| `MIPStarRE/`, `MIPStarRE.lean` | the Lean 4 development — the contribution |
    16	| `lakefile.toml`, `lake-manifest.json`, `lean-toolchain` | the pinned build: Lean 4 and all ten dependencies by exact revision |
    17	| `blueprint/src/` | the LaTeX blueprint, cross-referenced to the Lean names with `\lean{}` / `\leanok` |
    18	| `docs/` | the mathematical documentation, including `docs/QPBT-theorem-index.md` (every headline and supporting statement with its Lean name, blueprint label and paper locator) and `docs/paper-gaps/` (the register of gaps found in the source papers) |
    19	| `references/` | the TeX sources of the five source papers — third-party material, see below — so that the paper locators can be checked inside the snapshot; the report below records two existing exceptions |
    20	| `scripts/comparator/` | the generator for the self-contained `Challenge.lean` statement file used by the independent challenge repository |
    21	| `scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py` | the blueprint/axiom consistency check |
    22	| `scripts/make_artifact.sh` | the script that produced this snapshot, so the packaging is itself auditable |
    23	| `MANIFEST.txt` | source commit, file count, Lean code-line total, toolchain, Mathlib revision, leak-scan and self-containment results |
    24	
    25	## What is **not** in it, and why
    26	
    27	**The AI-workflow layer.** This development was produced with a local
    28	agent-orchestration layer: `local/`, `results/telemetry/`, `.github/` prompts
    29	and workflows, `.githooks/`, `audits/`, `home_page/`, `docbuild/`, and the
    30	scripts and docs that only serve that layer. It stays in the source repository
    31	because it is research material in its own right, but it is not part of the
    32	mathematics and it dominates the repository's size (the telemetry session logs
    33	alone are roughly 200 MB). Excluding it also removes, without any history
    34	rewrite, the ~2,456 tracked files that mention the build host's home path.
    35	
    36	## Third-party material: the paper sources, `references/`
    37	
    38	The snapshot ships the TeX sources of the five papers the development is
    39	formalized from (owner decision, 2026-09-19, following the companion
    40	low-degree-test repository, which likewise keeps its paper sources in the
    41	public repository):
    42	
    43	| path | paper | arXiv |
    44	|---|---|---|
    45	| `references/qpbt-paper/` | *MIP\* = RE* (primary source) | arXiv:2001.04383 |
    46	| `references/neexp-paper/` | *NEEXP in MIP\** (secondary source) | arXiv:1904.05870 |
    47	| `references/ldt-paper/` | low individual degree test | arXiv:2009.12982 |
    48	| `references/nv-paper/` | Natarajan–Vidick | arXiv:1610.03574 |
    49	| `references/cs-paper/` | see `references/cs-paper/SOURCE.md` | — |
    50	
    51	**Why they ship.** Lean docstrings and `docs/QPBT-theorem-index.md` cite their
    52	source as `references/<paper>/<file>.tex:<lines>`, and so will
    53	`docs/DEVIATIONS.md` when it lands (it is pending in another packet, and the
    54	two `README.md` links to it are the two dead internal-link occurrences that
    55	`MANIFEST.txt` still reports). With the sources in the snapshot all but the two
    56	locators listed below resolve inside the tarball, and a reviewer can read the
    57	paper statement next to the Lean statement without reconstructing the
    58	per-section split from arXiv. The directories are plain per-section splits of
    59	the papers' arXiv sources.
    60	
    61	**Licence.** These files are the work of their own authors and are **not**
    62	covered by the Apache-2.0 `LICENSE` that ships with the snapshot and governs the
    63	development itself. They are kept here for reference and for line-precise
    64	citation; their own terms govern any further use or redistribution. The
    65	`MANIFEST.txt` of every snapshot repeats this.
    66	
    67	**Locator report.** `MANIFEST.txt` records how many of the
    68	`references/<paper>/<file>.tex` paths cited in the Lean sources, the blueprint
    69	and the docs actually resolve inside the snapshot. It is a report, not a gate:
    70	a locator may name a section the per-file split arranges differently. The
    71	gap-note template's fill-in placeholder is not counted (the mirrors' file names
    72	are lower case, so a locator with a capital in it is a form to complete rather
    73	than a citation). At the commit named in the MANIFEST two do not resolve —
    74	`references/ldt-paper/commutativity_points.tex` and
    75	`references/ldt-paper/projectivization.tex`, cited from
    76	`MIPStarRE/LDT/CommutativityPoints/AnswerTheorems.lean` and
    77	`MIPStarRE/LDT/MakingMeasurementsProjective/Orthonormalization.lean`. They
    78	predate this packaging work and are tracked separately; the surrounding
    79	docstrings also name their blueprint labels, which do resolve.
    80	
    81	**Leak scan.** The scan that gates packaging (below) treats these files like
    82	any other: a home path or a key-shaped string inside `references/` still fails
    83	the run. The one forgiveness is scoped to `references/` by path and to
    84	e-mail addresses by content — the corresponding-author addresses printed in the
    85	papers' own front matter, which are third-party material reproduced as
    86	published, not contact addresses of this development. It is recorded as a
    87	`LEAK_ALLOW_IN` entry in `scripts/make_artifact.sh` with that reason, and a
    88	blanket entry was deliberately not used: the scan must still catch an address of
    89	ours anywhere else in the snapshot.
    90	
    91	## Verifying the artifact as a reviewer
    92	
    93	### 1. Install the pinned toolchain
    94	
    95	```sh
    96	curl https://elan.lean-lang.org/elan-init.sh -sSf | sh   # if elan is not installed
    97	cd <unpacked snapshot>
    98	cat lean-toolchain     # leanprover/lean4:v4.32.0 — elan installs this on first use
    99	```
   100	
   101	### 2. Fetch the Mathlib build cache and build
   102	
   103	```sh
   104	lake exe cache get
   105	lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT
   106	```
   107	
   108	**Expected cost.** `lake exe cache get` downloads several GB. Plan on **16 GB
   109	of RAM** and tens of GB of disk. At this source commit, these commands count
   110	occurrences and files, respectively:
   111	
   112	```sh
   113	rg -n -o 'maxHeartbeats' MIPStarRE | wc -l
   114	rg -l 'maxHeartbeats' MIPStarRE | wc -l
   115	rg -n -o 'synthInstance\.maxSize' MIPStarRE | wc -l
   116	rg -l 'synthInstance\.maxSize' MIPStarRE | wc -l
   117	```
   118	
   119	They report 38 occurrences across 23 files for `maxHeartbeats`, and 66 across
   120	17 files for `synthInstance.maxSize`, so this is not a laptop build. Honest
   121	statement of the evidence we have: the maintainers' build telemetry records
   122	1,608 builds of this development, but every one is an
   123	*incremental, warm-cache* build (the two most recent took 79 s and 556 s); the

   129	### 3. Check that nothing is assumed
   130	
   131	The development claims to depend on no axioms beyond Lean's three standard
   132	ones — `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` — and on no `sorry`,
   133	`admit`, `native_decide`, `unsafe` or `@[extern]` escape hatch.
   134	
   135	The check that settles the first half is Lean's own `#print axioms`: it reports
   136	the complete axiom closure of a declaration, and unlike a text search it cannot
   137	be misled by prose. The snapshot ships two modules that run it at build time and
   138	**fail the build** when a declaration's closure is not exactly
   139	`{Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext}` — one for the Pauli test, one for the
   140	classical low-individual-degree layer underneath it:
   141	
   142	```sh
   143	lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.AxiomAudit
   144	lake build MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit
   145	```
   146	
   147	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.AxiomAudit` covers the four headline theorems of section 4
   148	and nine further load-bearing statements; the printed axiom lines stay in the
   149	build log as the positive record. Neither module is imported from the
   150	`MIPStarRE.QPBT` umbrella — that keeps the audits out of ordinary downstream
   151	imports — so a plain `lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT` does not run them and they have
   152	to be named, as above.
   153	
   154	To read the closures directly instead, put this in a scratch file at the root of
   155	the unpacked snapshot and elaborate it with `lake env lean scratch.lean`:
   156	
   157	```lean
   158	import MIPStarRE.QPBT
   159	
   160	#print axioms MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness
   161	#print axioms MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit
   162	#print axioms MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one
   163	#print axioms MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness
   164	```
   165	
   166	Each of the four must report exactly `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.
   167	A `sorryAx` in a closure would mean the theorem is not proved; a project
   168	`axiom` would appear in the list under its own name.
   169	
   170	`#print axioms` does not report `native_decide`, `unsafe` or `@[extern]`, which
   171	move trust outside the kernel without leaving an axiom behind. A text search is
   172	the check for those, and for `axiom` declarations:
   173	
   174	```sh
   175	grep -rn --include='*.lean' -E '^[[:space:]]*axiom |\b(sorry|admit|native_decide|unsafe)\b|@\[extern' MIPStarRE/
   176	```
   177	
   178	**Expected output: a handful of matches, every one of them inside a comment or
   179	a docstring that discusses an escape hatch rather than using one.** At the
   180	commit named in `MANIFEST.txt` there are four: three are the word `sorry` in
   181	backticks — `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Apply.lean`, describing a source proof
   182	that was open in the paper, and the two audit modules named above, whose prose
   183	says what they exist to catch — and one is a docstring line in
   184	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/QubitForm.lean` that happens to begin with the word
   185	"axiom". A match in code position — a bare `sorry` in
   186	tactic position, or a line that really begins a declaration with `axiom` —
   187	would be a genuine escape hatch. `grep` cannot tell prose from code, which is
   188	why the `#print axioms` run above is the check that counts.

   224	
   225	```sh
   226	git tag -a itp-2027-artifact-v1 -m "ITP artifact snapshot"
   227	git push github itp-2027-artifact-v1
   228	scripts/make_artifact.sh itp-2027-artifact-v1 /tmp/artifact

   231	The script extracts the snapshot, builds the gap-note PDFs when
   232	`docs/paper-gaps/Makefile` is present, writes the MANIFEST, runs the leak scan,
   233	and prints the tarball path and its sha256. It **exits 2 without packaging**
   234	if the leak scan finds a home path, a key-shaped string or an e-mail address
   235	that is not allow-listed with a reason in the script.

   237	Then verify the snapshot the way a reviewer would, in a scratch directory and
   238	from the tarball alone — never in the working tree, whose Mathlib cache would
   239	mask a missing dependency:

   242	cd $(mktemp -d) && tar xzf /tmp/artifact/mipstarre-qpbt-artifact-*.tar.gz
   243	cd mipstarre-qpbt-artifact-* && lake exe cache get && lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT
