   249	### Double-blind venues
   250	
   251	ITP has historically been single-blind, and the target edition's call for
   252	papers governs. If a double-blind submission is ever needed:
   253	
   254	```sh
   255	scripts/make_artifact.sh --anonymize <tag> /tmp/artifact
   256	```
   257	
   258	This additionally rewrites the author-identifying strings listed in
   259	`ANON_RULES` in the script (the GitHub owner name inside URLs, the upstream
   260	project name and host, the author name and address) and tags the tarball
   261	`-anon`. The rewrite is not taken on trust: the script itself ships, so the
   262	pass runs over its own rules list as well, and before packaging anything the
   263	run searches the whole snapshot -- including the text extracted from every
   264	PDF, which `sed` cannot rewrite -- for each of those strings and exits `2`
   265	rather than package a survivor. It does **not** touch the source papers under
   266	`references/`, and it should not: those are published third-party works, and
   267	their authors are the cited paper authors, not the submitters. It is **not** by itself
   268	sufficient: the commit history, the issue and PR links in the docs, and the
   269	hosted blueprint would still identify the authors, so a double-blind
   270	submission needs a fresh single-commit repository built from the anonymized
   271	snapshot, not merely this flag.

   273	## Keeping the two exclusion lists in step
   274	
   275	What ships is decided twice, on purpose:
   276	
   277	- `INCLUDE` / `EXCLUDE` in `scripts/make_artifact.sh` — an explicit allow-list,
   278	  so a new top-level directory never joins the artifact by accident;
   279	- the `export-ignore` attributes in `.gitattributes` — applied by `git archive`
   280	  itself, so a plain `git archive` or a GitHub source tarball is clean too.
   281	
   282	A path excluded in one should be excluded in the other, and the second guard is
   283	the weaker of the two: it is a deny-list, so a new workflow-only file has to be
   284	added to it by hand, whereas the allow-list drops anything it has not been told
   285	about. `scripts/` is the one mixed directory — three entries ship, the roughly
   286	thirty workflow-only ones do not — and `git archive` does not descend into a
   287	directory it has been told to ignore, so a child of an ignored directory cannot
   288	be re-admitted. The deny-list therefore excludes the workflow-only scripts by
   289	glob (`scripts/*.py`, `scripts/*.sh`, `scripts/*.lean`, `scripts/tests/`) and
   290	re-admits the two shipped top-level files with `-export-ignore`;
   291	`scripts/comparator/` is never matched and ships under both guards.
   292	`references/` is named in `.gitattributes` too, as a comment rather than an
   293	`export-ignore` line, so that the decision to ship it is visible where somebody
   294	would otherwise add the line back. Checked again on 2026-09-21 at the final PR
   295	head: a plain `git archive` of the repository produces 872 files, while normal
   296	and anonymized `scripts/make_artifact.sh --no-pdf` snapshots each contain 873,
   297	the snapshot adding only its `MANIFEST.txt`. The retained full-PDF run used
   298	input-equivalent head `0e710bce16de`: `docs/paper-gaps/` is unchanged through
   299	the final head, and later included edits change only the contents of existing
   300	exported paths. That run built 49 gap-note PDFs and produced 922 files after
   301	pruning 339 `latexmk` intermediates. The PDFs are not tracked in git and so
   302	cannot appear in a plain `git archive`; the intermediates are pruned both
   303	because they are not part of the artifact and because `.fls` and
   304	`.fdb_latexmk` record the absolute path of the directory the build ran in.
   305	
   306	The leak scan is the backstop: it is what caught an upstream developer's home
   307	path in `docs/reports/` and got that directory excluded. It is fail-closed —
   308	exit 2, nothing packaged — and forgives a hit only through an entry that
   309	carries a written reason: `LEAK_ALLOW` for a pattern safe anywhere (the RFC 2606
   310	placeholder domains) and `LEAK_ALLOW_IN` for one safe only in named paths (the
   311	papers' own author addresses under `references/`). PDFs are covered too: any
   312	PDF in the snapshot has its text extracted with `pdftotext` and scanned with
   313	everything else, and the run stops rather than ship a PDF it could not read, so
   314	cutting a release with the gap notes built needs `poppler-utils` installed.

-`pauli_soundness` states: there are constants `a ≥ 1` and `0 < b < 1` such that
-for every admissible parameter tuple `P` and every `ε ≥ 0`, every strategy for
-the Pauli basis test with value at least `1 - ε` admits local isometries and an

-`deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q` of the ideal state, and both players' operator

-`deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ)`, `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/SoundnessDefs.lean:35` —

-the admissible sizes `m`, `d` and `q` as well as on `ε`, which is what the
-`q^(-b)` and `2^(-b·m·d)` terms express. As in the source, the constants are
-existentially quantified and no regime in which `deltaQld < 1` is exhibited;

+`pauli_soundness` states that universal constants `a >= 1` and `0 < b < 1`
+exist such that every admissible parameter tuple `P`, every `epsilon >= 0`, and
+every strategy winning the Pauli basis test with probability at least
+`1 - epsilon` admit local isometries and an auxiliary state. The state distance
+and both players' distances for the **raw prescribed-answer Pauli effects** are
+bounded by
+
+```text
+deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q
+  = a * (P.m * P.d)^a
+      * (epsilon^b + P.q^(-b) + 2^(-b * P.m * P.d)).
+```
